text(await tools.send_message({target:"/root",message:"Read-only exploration of clean /root/hevy-mcp main (2443cad) complete; no CONTEXT.md or ADRs found, worktree clean. Evidence-backed ranked deepening candidates (no concrete TS interfaces proposed):

1) Deep runtime-neutral MCP application/request host (strongest). `packages/core/src/server.ts:20-75` currently creates `McpServer`, client, catalog, `ToolRuntime`, and registers tools/prompts/resources, but accepts a broad options bag (`createClient`, observer/cache hooks, `decorateServer`, registration callback, timeout/deadline/lifecycle signal). Node repeats composition/lifecycle/telemetry in `packages/node/src/index.ts:247-301,414-497`; Worker repeats default server/transport/client composition in `packages/worker/src/worker.ts:208-244,323-352`. Both adapters have their own validation, deadline, connect, error, and cleanup paths. A deep application host could own server construction + request-scoped execution/cache identity while adapters retain only host-specific auth/transport/lifecycle. Preserve real stateless Worker vs stateful Node HTTP vs stdio differences. Deletion test: remove Node `buildServer`/Worker `createDefaultServer`+`serveMcpRequest` composition duplication while each transport still owns connect/handle/close.

2) Runtime-parity observability seam (strong). Core already has privacy-safe observer contract `packages/core/src/observation.ts:53-127` and cache observer `packages/core/src/utils/cache.ts:10-32`; client exposes request hooks `packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client-kubb.ts:76-128`. Node wires OTel/Sentry tool+cache+client observers in `packages/node/src/index.ts:264-277`, `packages/node/src/utils/tool-observer.ts:202-323`, `packages/node/src/utils/hevy-client-observability.ts:105-222`, plus SDK/private transport instrumentation. Worker’s default path (`worker.ts:220-225,228-244,323-350`) only passes `onLog`; no ToolObserver, CacheObserver, onRequestStart/onRequestComplete/onRetryWait, or SDK failure tracking. It does emit structured console events (`worker.ts:246-267,550-555`) and Cloudflare observability is enabled in `cloudflare.config.ts:20-53`, so the gap is application-level tool/API/cache correlation and failure parity, not “no Worker observability.” Deepen a runtime-specific telemetry adapter over the existing neutral events, using Cloudflare-native sinks rather than importing Node OTel. Deletion test: Worker can provide the same bounded event vocabulary without changing core or pulling Node packages.

3) Transport/protocol lifecycle seam (strong, but keep security local). Node HTTP module `packages/node/src/utils/streamable-http.ts` is 494 LOC and owns host validation, body limits, separate HTTP bearer auth, stateful session map, response tracking, disconnect abort, server/transport cleanup (`:23-45,92-220,231-494`). Worker `worker.ts:323-352` creates a fresh Web-standard transport/server per request and handles transport errors. Node stdio adds private SDK internals in `packages/node/src/utils/stdio-observability.ts:58-133,347-360`; Node SDK request-handler monkey-patching is in `packages/node/src/utils/sdk-observability.ts:114-300`; Worker has none. A deep protocol-host seam can isolate SDK-version details and common connect/close/error projection while leaving stateful/stateless transport implementations and auth/CORS in their adapters. Deletion test: remove duplicated `server.connect`/transport error/cleanup plumbing without forcing Worker sessions or Node sessions to share semantics.

4) API-key validation and execution-policy module (medium). Node startup probe `packages/node/src/index.ts:215-245` (one static env key; 401/403 -> startup error, network -> warning) and Worker per-request validation `packages/worker/src/worker.ts:292-320,389-429` (deadline-limited, 401/403 -> 401, upstream -> 502) duplicate upstream probe/classification; OAuth calls same Worker validator (`packages/worker/src/worker-oauth.ts:358-417,461-489`). Worker response status/outcome mapping is separate in `packages/worker/src/execution-response.ts:8-47`, while core owns projections (`packages/core/src/execution.ts:15-67`). Centralize only neutral validation/result/deadline classification; keep trust models adapter-local (Node env/static vs Worker bearer/OAuth and separate Node HTTP bearer). Deletion test: no repeated 401/403/deadline mapping, while no adapter shares the other’s credential storage/auth assumptions.

5) Re-evaluate `operations` depth (medium/high maintainability, not primarily transport). `packages/operations/src/index.ts:18-29` exposes only `workouts.list`; implementation is 101 LOC (`workouts.ts:10-101`). Most core tools still call `runtime.getClient()` directly (`packages/core/src/tools/workouts.ts:88-220`, `routines.ts`, `workflows.ts:158-260`, `routine-discovery.ts:21-70`, resources `packages/core/src/resources/hevy.ts:50-129`); CLI uses operations only for workouts list and direct client for remaining commands (`packages/cli/src/commands/index.ts:97-270`). This is either a shallow module to deepen into a coherent domain-operation layer (pagination, expected-404, workflows) or delete. Deletion test: deleting `operations` requires only direct client paths; deepening should remove repeated pagination/404 policy from core/CLI rather than layering wrappers.

6) Execution-context propagation seam (medium, high leverage). `packages/core/src/execution.ts:70-133` maintains a hand-updated `HEVY_CLIENT_OPTION_INDEXES` table and Proxy to inject signal/deadline into every curated client method; tests enumerate every method (`packages/core/src/execution.test.ts:9-93`). `ToolRuntime.forExecution` recursively rebuilds runtime and rebinds client (`packages/core/src/tools/tool-runtime.ts:163-295`); resources manually scope each MCP request (`packages/core/src/resources/hevy.ts:74-127`). Node and Worker both pass lifecycle/deadline through their server factories (`index.ts:264-276`, `worker.ts:228-237,331-336`). A deeper request execution module could make one request scope the leverage point and eliminate brittle option-slot bookkeeping; preserve neutral client semantics. Deletion test: adding/removing a client operation should not require synchronizing an index table across runtime and tests.

Contradictory/stale docs observed: `CONTRIBUTING.md:71-74` still says Node is stdio-only/no `--transport`, while actual `packages/node/src/index.ts:414-497` and `packages/node/src/utils/arguments.ts:61-110` support HTTP. README claims local Node HTTP shares an in-memory catalog across concurrent sessions (`packages/node/README.md:244-285`), but `streamable-http.ts:368-410` calls the server factory per initialize and `index.ts:452-462` builds a fresh server/catalog per session; likely per-session caches. `docs/architecture.md` also has stale 26-tool count. Treat as verification/documentation-locality issue, not proof of runtime bug.

Uncertainty: Cloudflare’s configured `observability` may capture platform traces/logs, but Worker code has no explicit application ToolObserver/client hooks; exact parity depends on destination behavior. Core’s broad options are intentionally runtime-neutral today, so narrowing them would be an architectural tradeoff, not an obvious defect."}));
